'''Konstanze Rietsch''' is a pure mathematician who was educated in Austria and the US. She works in the UK as Professor of Geometry at [[King's College London]].

==Research==
Rietsch's research concerns the geometry of [[Flag variety|flag varieties]] and  [[Mirror symmetry (string theory)|mirror symmetry]] in [[Lie theory]].{{r|pure}} 

==Education and career==
Rietsch received a master's degree in 1993 from the [[University of Vienna]] in 1993 and completed a Ph.D. in 1998 at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].{{r|pure}} Her doctoral dissertation, ''Total Positivity and Real Flag Varieties'', was supervised by [[George Lusztig]].{{r|mg}}

Following her doctorate, she visited the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey]],{{r|ias}} and became a postdoctoral research fellow in [[Newnham College, Cambridge]].{{r|newnham}} Next, she became a Violette and Samuel Glasstone Research Fellow at the [[Mathematical Institute, University of Oxford]].{{r|glasstone}}

She moved to King's College in 2002. 

==Recognition==
Rietsch is an invited speaker at the 2026 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].{{r|icm}}
